title: Harness of Minervini v2 ticker.risk response

examples: scripts/.venv/bin/python scripts/pipeline ticker risk AAPL --market-state favorable --eligibility-state eligible --setup-state ready --fundamentals-state supports_convergence --entry-price 200 --stop-price 188 --upside-price 224 --average-gain-pct 24
scripts/.venv/bin/python scripts/pipeline ticker risk AAPL --mode active --entry-price 200 --entry-date 2026-08-10 --stop-price 188

exit_codes.0: A valid domain envelope was emitted; its status may still be partial, unavailable, or needs_input.
exit_codes.2: The request or arguments were invalid; stdout contains a needs_input error envelope.
exit_codes.3: An unexpected internal contract failure occurred; stdout contains an unavailable error envelope.

as_of.description: Completed US trading session in YYYY-MM-DD form; defaults to the latest completed regular session.

average_gain_pct.description: The trader's realized average gain percentage. Prospective mode cannot reach BUY-READY without it; its absence is reported as missing evidence, not a relaxed cap. In active mode it is one of the two reference points for selling into strength, reported as a distance from the position's return and never as a trigger.

base_count.description: How many bases this stage 2 advance has formed, counted by the analyst. It is reported against the three-to-five range the source names for a typical top, together with the source's own disclaimer that base counting cannot say a stock has topped. It never becomes an action.

base_top.description: The top of the base the position broke out from. With it, the last close's extension over the base top is reported against the 20-25 pause zone TraderLion describes, and sitting inside that zone is a tagged REVIEW action; past it or short of it is evidence only.

breakout_date.description: The session of the breakout. It anchors the since-breakout windows: the key-reversal criteria, the gap-up count and the latest gap's fate, and the breakout session's volume ratio against the fifty sessions before it -- a later down session heavier than the breakout session is the sell-or-reduce REVIEW Minervini describes. Every one of them is doctrine about what a stock does after it breaks out, so without this date they are reported unavailable under breakout_date_not_declared rather than measured from the entry session -- an early or cheat entry has not broken out yet, and reading post-breakout behavior into it would answer a question the doctrine never asked. The same withholding applies to the pause-zone review that --base-top raises.

completed_stop_breach.description: Assert a stop breach on completed evidence.

current_price.description: Optional explicit latest completed price. A value at or below the stop can trigger SELL, but a value above it cannot establish HOLD without the provider-audited completed price path.

earnings_date.description: The next earnings report for this position. A report still ahead of --as-of is a REVIEW action: Minervini tells a holder to be aware of the coming report and of the same industry group's, and the harness reports beside it that Zanger, a practitioner it reads for contrast, has not held through a release in more than ten years. A report already behind the position is evidence only.

entry_date.description: Actual ISO entry date; required in active mode.

entry_price.description: Positive planned or actual entry price.

format.description: Output detail only; compact preserves verdict, signals, and missing evidence while omitting verbose basis rows.

initial_stop_price.description: The hard stop the trade started with, for when --stop-price has since been raised. Initial risk is entry minus this, and R multiples and 3R protection are measured from it; without it a raised stop leaves R unmeasured rather than measured from the wrong risk. Declaring it beside a different --stop-price requires --stop-effective-date, because a raised stop was raised on some date.

invalidation_condition.description: Observable structural invalidation condition. Pair it with --invalidation-price in active mode: a condition the harness cannot evaluate against completed bars is reported as missing evidence rather than assumed unbreached.

invalidation_price.description: Positive structural invalidation price. In active mode it is audited over completed bars from --entry-date, alongside and independently of the hard stop.

live_stop_breach.description: Assert a live breach; SELL requires live_stop_check too.

management_average.description: The moving average the trader manages the position by, declared as their own exit plan: ema21 for swing management, sma50 for a position trail (the TraderLion role split). Two completed closes below it, both inside the position, are audited over completed bars like a stop and are a SELL. Both averages are measured either way; the one not declared reports two closes below it as a REVIEW action.

management_profile.description: Opt into a tagged TraderLion practice-layer management default. tl_stage12 is the Stage 1 and 2 rule: once the position has shown a 5 percent profit, REDUCE half and RAISE_STOP to breakeven. A profile adds management_actions under HOLD, each marked binds false and source [TL], and never touches the verdict.

no_cache.description: Bypass both provider-cache reads and writes for this invocation.

stage2_start.description: The session the stage 2 advance began. With it, the largest daily and weekly decline since then are measured and the latest completed session or week being that decline is a REVIEW action that needs the chart; without it that block is reported unavailable rather than measured from an arbitrary start.

stop_effective_date.description: Calendar date when --stop-price became effective in active mode; defaults to --entry-date. The audit begins with the first completed bar on or after this date.

stop_price.description: Positive hard-stop price. In active mode, every completed daily Low is audited from the stop's effective date through --as-of.

upside_price.description: Positive evidence-based reward reference; required in prospective mode.

limitations: This capability never recommends portfolio allocation or position size. A REDUCE action names a fraction of the position, which is a selling discipline, not an allocation.
A hard stop may not exceed 10% or half the realized average gain; --average-gain-pct is required for a prospective verdict and reward-to-risk must be at least 2:1.

A completed current price above the protective level cannot establish HOLD: the provider must cover every completed daily Low from --stop-effective-date through --as-of; a recovered price does not erase an earlier breach.

Each protective level is audited from its own effective date: the hard stop from --stop-effective-date, the structural invalidation from --entry-date. A breach of either is a SELL, and HOLD requires every declared level to be cleared over its whole window.
--stop-effective-date defaults to --entry-date. When a stop was raised or replaced later, supply its actual effective date so the newer stop is not applied retroactively.

Active-mode chronology is checked before any evidence is fetched: --entry-date cannot follow --as-of, and --stop-effective-date can neither precede --entry-date nor follow --as-of. An asserted breach outranks evidence nobody gathered, but never a request that contradicts itself or declares no exit plan.
An explicit --current-price at or below the stop can trigger SELL; a partial-session breach must instead use the explicit live-stop flags.
A live stop breach triggers SELL only when --live-stop-check is explicit; ordinary gates use completed bars.

A completed breach records the breaching session's Open and whether it opened below the level (gap_through_stop): a stop the market gapped through was never available at its price, and the record does not pretend it was. A breach also names the level it is about in governing_role: price falls from above, so among the levels one session or one price broke, the record is about the highest -- the line it crossed first -- and only a level whose own window still reaches --as-of can be broken by a price printed today. A breached invalidation and a breached stop are both a SELL and are not the same finding. An explicit --current-price at or below one level says only that: a level below it is reported unaudited rather than clear, since one price cannot say what a session last week did.
The reducer does not infer unsupported market, eligibility, setup, or fundamentals states.

Two closes below --management-average sell because the trader declared that average as their exit plan, not because TraderLion's rule binds this harness; the same two closes below the average not declared are a REVIEW action. A declared average the bars cannot read (too little history) leaves HOLD unestablished, like an unaudited stop.

Weeks are read to the Friday. A trailing week with no Friday session is not promoted to completed -- without a trading calendar an exchange holiday and an unfinished week look the same -- but it is published beside the finding as pending_week_ending with its own change, so a week the block declined to weigh is never silently dropped. A close below the 20-day average and the largest decline of the advance are REVIEW evidence, never a SELL on their own: the source calls the first a judgment call and the second a sell signal in most cases, and keeps the hard stop as the only automatic exit.

One stop raise is expressible: --initial-stop-price with --stop-effective-date splits the audit into the level that governed before the raise and the level in force since. A position whose stop moved twice cannot be described here, and the intermediate level is not audited.

A window is only as good as the bars inside it. The audit reports the first and last bar it actually read, and an --entry-date the provider printed no bar for makes the position unauditable rather than clear -- a stop may be moved on a day the market was shut, but a position cannot be opened on one. Sessions missing in the middle of a window cannot be told from market holidays without a trading calendar, which this harness does not carry.

A structure measurement is unavailable rather than approximated: a frame carrying a NaN or non-positive price, a --breakout-date with no completed bar, a history that begins after the window it is asked about, and a provider frame without Open or Volume each name what is missing instead of publishing a number computed around it.

Prices are the ones the tape printed, unadjusted, with the split events beside them. A share split inside an audit or measurement window puts the declared entry and stop in one coordinate system and the closes in another, so the window is refused from the event onward rather than measured across -- a breach the audit already found before it stands, because an event two sessions later cannot un-take-out a stop the market took out. Each measurement asks about its own window: a split before the sessions a simple average reads is outside it, while the recursive average runs from the first bar and spans everything. A refusal names the sessions it did read before the event, and a declared exit those sessions already triggered is published as the breach it was. The refusal reports the window unavailable rather than measured across -- including the current price, which would otherwise sell a position the market never took out. A history that carries no split column has not said there was no split, so a close-to-close change of a fifth or more -- the ratio of a five-for-four, the smallest ordinary split -- is refused the same way under corporate_action_evidence_missing: the harness cannot tell a share count changing from a fall the market made, and the two call for opposite answers. The highest High since entry is withheld on the same finding, under max_high_withheld_reason, because three R measured across an event is a gain the position never had.

Post-breakout doctrine needs --breakout-date. The 20-day rule the source states begins "Once the stock successfully breaks out" and the pause zone is an extension a stock pauses at after breaking out, so both publish their measurement with the reason the action was withheld beside it. The tennis-ball behavior, the first sessions out of the base, the gaps since the breakout and the key-reversal criteria have nothing to measure without it and are unavailable outright. A declared date the bars cannot find -- no completed session printed on it, or the returned history begins after it -- is not an anchor either, and the actions are withheld under that reason rather than the date being taken on trust.

The favorable excursion is measured from the session after entry: a daily bar cannot say whether its High printed before or after the fill, and crediting the entry session's own spike would raise a stop and cut a position on a gain that never happened. The last completed close remains the floor of what was reached.

Market weakness can raise a stop and can never sell a position: the source tightens stops and lets price action take him out one position at a time. The sizing half of the same passage -- reduce exposure with regard to position sizes -- is deliberately not implemented, because this capability never prescribes size.

Two fields say different things about what a block did not read. missing_inputs names evidence the block wanted and the history did not hold -- a column that is absent, or a session whose value is unusable. claim_inputs_not_read names evidence the cited claim lists that this particular reading never consumes: the climax vector measures price and volume and never the base count, and the base-count disclaimer is quoted beside a declared count without reading price or volume history. An INCOMPLETE active verdict carries no management_evidence: those measurements are keyed to a position the request never established. A SELL keeps them, because there the position was real and the structure is part of why it ended.
x-capability-contract.output: The sole final ticker verdict with component states, completed stop-path evidence, failed/waiting/missing evidence, stop constraints, reward-to-risk, and 3R protection context. An active HOLD also carries management_actions -- what to do while holding, each naming its action (RAISE_STOP, REDUCE, or REVIEW), the claim it comes from, and the measurement behind it; the list is empty when nothing is due, and SELL and INCOMPLETE carry no actions because there is nothing left to manage or no established position to manage. Beside them, management_evidence holds the structural measurements the actions were read from -- both management averages with their two-close audit and, at a breach, the quality of the second close (distance from the average, closing range, whether it held above the first close and the first low); the 20-day average against the last close; and, given --stage2-start, the largest daily and weekly decline of the advance with the session's volume ratio -- so a HOLD with an untouched stop and deteriorating structure reads as HOLD plus REVIEW, never as a bare HOLD. Given --base-top and --breakout-date it also measures selling-into-strength context: the extension over the base top against the 20-25 pause zone, the extension from each management average in percent and ATR beside the stock's own history of extensions, the six key-reversal criteria (three computed, three unresolved -- two are chart readings and the sixth asks for a close low in the range the source never bounds), the gap-ups since the breakout and the latest gap's fate, short-horizon returns with the last session's volume rank, and whether a down session since the breakout was heavier than the breakout session itself. These are measurements with their claims beside them; only the pause zone and the heavier-selling event become REVIEW actions, and none of them can sell. Time is evidence too: the block reports the sessions since entry, the sessions since the last new closing high, every natural reaction since the breakout with its depth and how long recovery took, and the first two sessions out of the base that Zanger reads for volume and price -- the tennis-ball reading Minervini describes, measured and left to the analyst. A declared --market-state of cautious or defensive raises the stop toward the five-to-six percent loss range the source cuts at in a difficult environment and never sells the ticker on an opinion of the market. Two more blocks are context the caller declares: --earnings-date still ahead of --as-of is a REVIEW carrying the contrast that one practitioner never holds through a release at all, and --base-count is reported against the three-to-five band with the source's own disclaimer that counting bases cannot call a top. A stage 3 vector travels with every active verdict that has a position -- the recent average true range against the earlier one, and the 200-session average's slope -- as measurements a chart reading is meant to finish, never as an action. Breakeven protection is reported rather than ordered once price has come back through it: a stop above the last completed close is a sale, not a stop, so risk_controls carries breakeven_protection_not_placeable instead of a RAISE_STOP. Three R is measured from the highest completed High since the entry session (max_high_since_entry, with its date), not from the last close: a gain that was reached and given back is exactly what the rule protects, and the last close is only the floor of what was reached when no High is available. Every limit comes from the doctrine registry: a gate decides pass or fail, while a band such as the ordinary loss target reports the measurement, the source's range, where the measurement sat against that range, and which edge of it is the good one -- a stop tighter than the range is outside it on the favourable side.
prerequisites: Prospective mode should consume market.snapshot, ticker.qualify, ticker.setup, and ticker.fundamentals verdicts.

status_meanings.needs_input: Required evidence is missing, so the domain verdict is INCOMPLETE.
status_meanings.ok: A complete BUY-READY, WAIT, AVOID, HOLD, or SELL verdict was produced; active HOLD includes a clear completed stop path.
status_meanings.partial: The completed-price provider failed, could not cover the full active stop window, or stopped before the requested session.
status_meanings.unavailable: An internal required capability cannot be evaluated.

x-capability-contract.summary: Reduce converged prospective evidence to BUY-READY, WAIT, AVOID, or INCOMPLETE, or active-position evidence to HOLD, SELL, or INCOMPLETE.
